stem: A nightly run of 50 models fails at `fct_reviews` due to a transient database timeout, after 30 models had already succeeded and before 19 others ran at all. The developer fixes the connectivity issue and runs `dbt retry`. The team needs to know exactly how many models dbt attempts to build on this retry. How many?

option_texts.A: 20, the failed model plus the models that never got a chance to run, since retry resumes from the point of failure
option_texts.B: 50, every model in the original selection, since retry always re-executes the full original invocation
option_texts.C: 30, the models that already succeeded, since retry re-validates every prior success
option_texts.D: 0, because a transient database timeout means there are no recorded nodes to retry from

drill_answer_short: Retry resumes from the point of failure, covering the failed node plus anything that hadn't run yet
decision_hinge: Retry re-executes the last invocation from the point of failure. Once some nodes have run, you can use retry to re-execute from any new point of failure.

plausible_options.C: after 30 models had already succeeded and before 19 others ran at all

eliminated_by.B: The developer fixes the connectivity issue and runs `dbt retry`

D.signal: after 30 models had already succeeded and before 19 others ran at all
D.requires_fact: If no nodes are executed before the failure there are no recorded nodes to retry from; here, 30 nodes already ran successfully before the failure, so this case does not apply.

distractor_traps.B: T4: breaks a stated fact — retry resumes from the point of failure, it does not re-run an already-successful invocation from scratch
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling — retry resumes forward from the failure, it does not re-validate a model that already succeeded
distractor_traps.D: T3: confusable sibling — the no-recorded-nodes case applies only when the failure happens before anything runs, not after 30 successes

stem: A CI pipeline should only build and test models changed in a pull request, plus their downstream dependents, using a production manifest artifact available at `prod-artifacts/`. The team needs the single `--select` expression that achieves this precise scope. Which selector is correct?

option_texts.A: `state:modified+ --state prod-artifacts/`, selecting modified nodes plus their descendants, compared against the production manifest
option_texts.B: `+state:modified --state prod-artifacts/`, selecting modified nodes plus their ancestors
option_texts.C: `state:modified --state prod-artifacts/`, selecting only the modified nodes against the production manifest, no further scope needed
option_texts.D: `@state:modified --state prod-artifacts/`, selecting modified nodes plus ancestors of their descendants too

drill_answer_short: A trailing + on state:modified includes descendants, which is what this CI scope needs
decision_hinge: Placed after a model/resource, the + operator includes the resource itself and all its descendants (downstream dependencies).

plausible_options.D: plus their downstream dependents, using a production manifest artifact available at `prod-artifacts/`

eliminated_by.B: plus their downstream dependents, using a production manifest artifact available at `prod-artifacts/`

C.requires_fact: Placed after a model/resource, the + operator includes the resource itself and all its descendants; without it, only the modified nodes themselves would be selected.

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling — a leading + selects ancestors (upstream), the opposite of the downstream dependents this CI job needs
distractor_traps.C: T4: breaks a stated requirement — the stem explicitly needs downstream dependents included too, which bare state:modified omits
distractor_traps.D: T7: over-engineering — @ additionally pulls in ancestors of descendants, useful for a different CI concern than simply building changed models and their dependents

stem: After a `dbt run`, dbt writes an artifact to the `target/` directory containing the execution time and status for every node in that invocation. Name this JSON artifact file: ____
drill_answer_short: run_results.json records timing and status info for each executed node
decision_hinge: This file contains information about a completed invocation of dbt, including timing and status info for each node that was executed.

stem: A Snowflake CI pipeline runs `dbt clone --state prod-artifacts/ --select +state:modified` as its first step, before the rest of the job runs tests. The team needs to know exactly why this step exists, what it prevents on a platform like Snowflake. What's the documented purpose?

option_texts.A: It clones modified incremental models' upstream ancestors cheaply up front, preventing a costly full-refresh build for warehouses that support zero-copy cloning
option_texts.B: It permanently deletes any model not selected by `+state:modified`, keeping the CI schema small
option_texts.C: It runs the full test suite immediately, using the production data as a substitute for CI data
option_texts.D: It replaces `--defer` entirely, so the job no longer needs a `--state` flag on later steps

drill_answer_short: Cloning modified incremental models' ancestors up front avoids a costly full-refresh, on zero-copy-capable platforms
decision_hinge: You may want to clone your modified incremental models as the first step of your dbt CI job to prevent costly full-refresh builds for warehouses that support zero-copy cloning.

plausible_options.C: before the rest of the job runs tests

eliminated_by.B: runs `dbt clone --state prod-artifacts/ --select +state:modified` as its first step
eliminated_by.D: before the rest of the job runs tests

distractor_traps.B: T1: fabricated — dbt clone copies selected nodes into the target schema, it does not delete anything
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling — cloning objects into a schema is not the same action as running a test suite against them
distractor_traps.D: T3: confusable sibling — dbt clone itself relies on the --defer feature, it does not replace the need for --state elsewhere in the job

stem: A team of 5 developers each needs to write to their own isolated schema during development, without manually configuring a different schema name for every model. The platform engineer needs the TWO configuration elements that genuinely achieve this by default. Which TWO are correct?

option_texts.A: Each developer's own `profiles.yml` target sets their personal `schema`, which the generate_schema_name macro uses as the base
option_texts.B: dbt's default `generate_schema_name` macro combines the target schema with any custom schema, so each developer's models land under their own target schema automatically
option_texts.C: Every model must set an explicit `schema:` config pointing at that one developer's name, repeated per model
option_texts.D: A single shared `dbt_project.yml` schema setting is what dbt uses by default, applying identically to every developer regardless of their own profile

drill_answer_short: Each developer's own target.schema, combined by the default generate_schema_name macro, isolates them automatically
decision_hinge: dbt uses a default macro called generate_schema_name to determine the name of the schema that a model should be built in. By default, dbt concatenates the target schema and the custom schema.

plausible_options.C: without manually configuring a different schema name for every model

eliminated_by.D: without manually configuring a different schema name for every model

distractor_traps.C: T7: over-engineering — a per-model, per-developer schema override is unnecessary when the default macro already isolates by target.schema
distractor_traps.D: T4: breaks a stated requirement — a single shared setting cannot isolate developers from each other by definition

stem: During a `dbt build`, a `not_null` test on `fct_reviews.reviewer_name` fails with `severity: error`. `mart_fullmoon_reviews` depends on `fct_reviews`. The team needs to know exactly what happens to `mart_fullmoon_reviews` in this same invocation. What happens?

option_texts.A: `mart_fullmoon_reviews` is skipped, because a test failure on an upstream resource blocks and skips its downstream resources
option_texts.B: `mart_fullmoon_reviews` still builds normally, since the test failure is isolated to `fct_reviews` alone
option_texts.C: `mart_fullmoon_reviews` builds, but with a warning logged alongside the test failure
option_texts.D: The entire `dbt build` invocation aborts immediately, stopping every other unrelated model too

drill_answer_short: A failing error-severity test on an upstream resource skips its downstream dependents
decision_hinge: Tests on upstream resources will block downstream resources from running, and a test failure will cause those downstream resources to skip entirely.

B.requires_fact: A test failure will cause those downstream resources to skip entirely; the failure is not isolated to only the model the test is attached to.

distractor_traps.B: T4: breaks a stated fact — a failing test blocks and skips downstream resources, it is not isolated to its own model
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated — a skip is not the same as a successful build with a warning attached
distractor_traps.D: T3: confusable sibling — aborting the whole invocation is --fail-fast behaviour, not the default skip rule for one failing test
